articles.title: Moments after Mini Cooper killed 3 students near Kochi airport: ‘Dad will handle’ - Moneycontrol.com
articles.full_text:
A 19-year-old has been arrested on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder after three youths were killed when his Mini Cooper rammed their scooter on the airport road at Nedumbassery near Kochi early on Sunday, TOI reported.
#WATCH | Keralam | Three students killed in an accident involving a car and a scooter in Nedumbassery, Kochi. The police have detained the car driver, Suhail Sajeev, and registered a case.Visuals of the vehicles involved in the accident (11.10) https://t.co/eZRvm1ULuh — ANI (@ANI) October 12, 2026
Police had to use force to protect the driver, identified as Suhail Sajeev, son of Alappuzha South native Sajeev Jamal, from an angry crowd at a hospital. The report said people confronted Suhail when police took him in for a medical examination.
His co-passenger, Ninav (19), reportedly had told first responders that his father will take care of things. Some people at the hospital asked Suhail where his father was. Ninav has also been arrested. The crash took place around 1.45 am, and police said Suhail was allegedly inebriated, as per the report.
According to the report, CCTV footage showed the premium hatchback hitting the scooter from behind, throwing the riders off on impact. The scooter landed some distance away and the front of the car was badly mangled. Locals rushed the youths to Desom CA hospital and Angamaly Taluk Hospital, where they were declared dead.
Police identified the victims as Devika (21) of Wayanad, Gopika (22) of Palakkad and Iyas (21) of Coorg in Karnataka. Nedumbassery police said the trio worked at a craft shop in Thrikkakara. They had gone to a tea shop near the airport and were on their way to Athani when the car hit them.
District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) KS Sudarshan said police took Suhail into custody from the spot and had his medical examination done immediately. Blood and urine samples were collected for forensic testing. He said the blood report was awaited, but the preliminary probe indicated that Suhail was inebriated. Asked whether other intoxicants were involved, he said samples had been taken to check this and further action would follow the medical reports.
The report noted that videos from an Instagram page purportedly belonging to Suhail were widely shared soon after the crash. One of them, an Instagram story, showed a car travelling at 220km/hr during a highway ride. Sudarshan said police had taken note of it and would investigate the driver’s background.
“Prima facie, the accused was drunk at the time. We have collected his blood and urine samples for confirmation. We will also check if he had consumed any narcotic substances. We have cameras on these routes. If such activities happened in the past, we will investigate them,” the Rural SP said.
The SP said police would also look into public concerns that car races take place in the region. He said witnesses reported that the car was speeding and police suspect the speed was over 120km/hr. A detailed forensic examination of the car has been carried out.
Police will record statements on reports that Suhail’s co-passenger had quarrelled with first responders, Sudarshan said. He added that more sections could be added against Suhail as and when further offences are established. Meanwhile, the excise department has begun an inquiry into bars that allegedly served alcohol to Suhail, who is below the legal drinking age of 23, the report said.
